questions.stem: A 52-year-old man presented with a 3-week history of watery diarrhea and abdominal cramping. He reported 6–8 watery bowel movements per day, cramping abdominal pain, and 25 lb weight loss. He was known to have HIV , hypertension, type 2 diabetes, and hypercholesterolemia. He was not taking antiretroviral therapy or antibiotic prophylaxis. On examination, there was diffuse abdominal tenderness and hyperactive bowel sounds but no peritoneal signs. Investigations: CD4 count 45 cells/μL HIV viral load 145,850 copies/mL Stool microscopy: multiple 4–6 μm oocysts that stain positive with modified acid-fast staining
questions.lead_in: What is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.explanation: Antiretroviral therapy The patient’s clinical presentation is consistent with diarrhea associated with Cryptosporidium, which is identified by modified acid-fast staining of stool demonstrating 4-6 μm oocysts. Because there is no proven effective treatment for this disease, immediate antiretroviral therapy (ART) is imperative to achieve immune restoration. Nitazoxanide is an effective treatment in immunocompetent patients and may offer some benefit but only as an adjunct to ART initiation. The other treatments are not active against this pathogen.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 8 Q22

questions.question: Cyclospora.

parts.text: What type of organism is this?

parts_raw.text: A) What type of organism is this?

questions.model_answer:
a) A coccidian protozoan parasite (phylum Apicomplexa, family Eimeriidae); species Cyclospora cayetanensis, an obligate intracellular enteric pathogen whose oocysts must sporulate in the environment to become infective.
b) TMP-SMX is the treatment of choice: 1 double-strength tablet (160 mg TMP/800 mg SMX) PO bid for 7 days in immunocompetent hosts and 7-10 days in HIV infection. HIV-infected patients often need suppressive therapy (TMP-SMX 1 DS three times weekly for 4 weeks) because of a ~50% relapse rate. For TMP-SMX intolerance: ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO bid for 7 days (slightly less efficacious, with reported failures); nitazoxanide 500 mg PO bid for 7 days is an alternative.
questions.beyond_mandell: The classification of Cyclospora as a coccidian protozoan (Apicomplexa, family Eimeriidae) is standard parasitology; the read slice covers therapy but does not state the taxonomy explicitly.

cohort_answer.text: Protozoa (sporozoa more specific); coccidian in phylum Apicomplexa, family Eimeriidae. Treatment: TMP-SMX 1 DS BID for 7 days if normal immune system, 7-10 days in HIV; if HIV may need suppressive therapy with TID dosing x4 weeks, then suppression TMP-SMX 3x weekly. Alternatives: Cipro 500mg BID x7 days (failures reported); Nitazoxanide 500mg BID x7 days.

questions.question: The current algorithm for intestinal parasites includes direct smears plus a concentration step and then an iron-hematoxylin (permanent trichrome-type) stain.
questions.question_raw: Current algorithm for intestinal parasites includes direct smears as well as concentrate and then iron hematoxylin stain.

parts.text: Name 4 clinically significant intestinal parasites that can be missed by this algorithm and 1 stain for each that you would use to detect them.

parts_raw.text: Name 4 clinically significant intestinal parasites that can be missed by this algorithm and 1 stain for each that you would use for them.

questions.model_answer: a) The routine ova-and-parasite algorithm (direct smear + formalin-ethyl-acetate concentration + iron-hematoxylin/trichrome permanent stain) does not reliably detect the intestinal coccidia or microsporidia, because their oocysts/spores stain poorly with iodine or trichrome and resemble yeast. Four missed pathogens and a dedicated stain for each: (1) Cryptosporidium spp. - modified acid-fast stain (modified Ziehl-Neelsen or Kinyoun; oocysts stain pink/red on a green-blue background), or auramine-rhodamine fluorescent stain / direct immunofluorescence. (2) Cyclospora cayetanensis - modified acid-fast stain (variably acid-fast; also autofluoresces under UV). (3) Cystoisospora (Isospora) belli - modified acid-fast stain. (4) Microsporidia (e.g., Enterocytozoon bieneusi, Encephalitozoon intestinalis) - modified trichrome stain (chromotrope 2R / Weber stain) or calcofluor white.
questions.beyond_mandell: Cyclospora, Cystoisospora and the microsporidian-specific stains (chromotrope 2R / calcofluor white) are established diagnostic practice (CDC DPDx; Mandell parasite-diagnosis chapters) rather than detailed in this Cryptosporidium chapter, which names acid-fast staining for Cryptosporidium and notes acid-fast stains also detect Cystoisospora and Cyclospora.
